correctness.rationale: The infinite-switching case gives two unbounded complementary subsets whose diamonds are top and whose four-element Boolean algebra is modal-closed. For finitely many switches, the Boolean algebra of maximal constant runs is modal-closed. Starting from the complement of the eventual tail, repeated diamond/intersection with the opposite color recovers every finite-run prefix, hence every atom. All cases, including zero switches, are covered without computational extrapolation. The standalone checker tests 510 ultimately constant generators.

broader_coverage.reasoning: Shapirovsky Theorem 1 covers finite powers and Agnew Theorem 3.16 covers transitive-frame local finiteness. Neither higher generality automatically specifies exact sizes or the atomic partition. Their coverage of mere finiteness does not subsume the quantitative claim.

They cannot entail the exact function of switching number or the distinction between finite- and infinite-switching generators without the new additional structural argument.

value.rationale: On a canonical infinite locally finite K4/S4 complex algebra, the theorem computes the full exact one-generator cardinality and atomic structure directly from its valuation pattern. It shows unbounded finite one-generator sizes yet a surprising four-element collapse for infinitely switching valuations, quantifying what the qualitative local-finiteness theorem cannot. The invariant is intrinsic to the accessibility order and all powers of two are sharp realizable sizes.
